Research / DigiGuard

DigiGuard

A modular wearable for adaptive finger tremor stabilization using elastic modulation: an affordable device that suppresses finger tremors by purely mechanical means.

Role
Mechanical design and testing
Timeline
Feb – May 2026

Try it: add a tremor

Move across the line to make it shake, then watch it steady.

The problem

People with neurodegenerative diseases often have finger tremors that reduce grip and comfort. Existing options, like stabilizing gloves, neuroprosthetics, and medication, don’t directly target finger tremors.

What I built

I designed and tested the mechanical dampening system and finalized the arm brace. Across four designs, we moved from a passive spring to an Arduino and accelerometer that detect a tremor and trigger a servo to tension a spring on the finger, with a delay to prevent false alarms. An engineering matrix selected the final design.

Results

Welch’s t-test on 1,464 accelerometer measurements over 5 engaged and disengaged cycles showed a statistically significant difference, with an 84% tremor reduction. Volunteers who simulated tremors rated it highly. Drawbacks were bulk, assembly difficulty, and restricted finger use.

DigiGuard’s fourth concept, a glove using MR fluid, became the starting point for StabiliQ, a new design built on a different principle.
